Front Porch Recovery

Front Porch Recovery — One honest day at a time

Pull up a chair.
You belong here.

A place for people rebuilding their lives. Recovery. Real life. Second chances. Hard conversations. Dumb jokes. Accountability. Hope. And learning how to live again — one honest day at a time.

Rough day?

You don't have to clean yourself up before you come through the door.

Maybe today was good. Maybe you barely made it through. Maybe you're sober, trying to get sober, supporting somebody you love, rebuilding after everything fell apart, or just trying to figure out what the hell comes next. Whatever brought you here, there's a seat for you.

This isn't a perfect-people porch

People deserve dignity. People also deserve honesty.

We believe in accountability without humiliation. Support without rescuing. Compassion without pretending consequences don't exist. And recovery that makes room for different paths, different stories, and different people. We're not here to tell you how your story is supposed to look — we're here to remind you that you can keep writing it. One honest day at a time.

Find your seat on the porch

You don't have to know exactly what you need. Start wherever feels right.

From the porch

Recovery isn't the only thing we talk about around here — because eventually, life gets bigger than recovery. Music, stories, humor, family, work, fear, dogs doing ridiculous things, unexpected good days, bad days that somehow end, and the strange realization that somewhere along the way, you started living again.

Recovery doesn't always have to sound like a meeting.

Sometimes it sounds like:

  • "I'm struggling today."
  • "I need somebody to talk to."
  • "I screwed up."
  • "I handled that better than I used to."
  • "I need a boundary."
  • "I need help."
  • "I'm proud of myself."
  • "I'm scared."
  • "I'm still here."

Around here, still here counts.

Why Front Porch Recovery exists

There comes a point when surviving isn't enough anymore.

You survived addiction. You survived the wreckage. You survived consequences, loss, shame, fear, relationships falling apart, and mornings you weren't sure you wanted to face. Then comes the strange part: learning how to live. Front Porch Recovery exists for that part too — the rebuilding, the awkward middle, the laughter coming back, the relationships, the responsibility, the ordinary Tuesday afternoon when you realize your life isn't on fire anymore. That matters.

Pull up a chair.

You don't need the right words. You don't need a perfect recovery story. You don't need to have everything figured out. Just show up honestly. We'll start there.

Porch Stories

My Story

Why the porch, and why me.

Front Porch Recovery didn't start as a business plan. It started on an actual porch, on an actual hard night, when staying sober for one more day was the only goal that felt possible.

Everything here comes out of lived experience — addiction, consequences, rebuilding a life one piece at a time, and learning the difference between helping someone and rescuing them. Surviving the storm turned out to be the beginning, not the end.

I write books, make music, and show up as a Certified Peer Support Specialist, because recovery needed more than one door to walk through. None of that matters more than this: I know what it's like to rebuild a life after addiction, consequences, and years spent surviving.

We're friendly. We're not here to pretend everything is fine.

People deserve dignity. People also deserve honesty. Accountability doesn't require humiliation, and helping someone doesn't mean removing every consequence from their life. Recovery belongs to the person living it — always has, always will.

Published author Certified Peer Support Specialist Songwriter

Okay. Today sucks.
Let's get through the next few minutes first.

You don't need to fix everything right now. Just the next hour.

Slow your breathing for a minute

Follow the circle. In as it grows, out as it shrinks.

Inhale

Inhale slowly for 4 seconds. Exhale slowly for 4 seconds. Repeat for as long as it helps.

Get grounded

Name, out loud or in your head:

  • • 5 things you can see
  • • 4 things you can touch
  • • 3 things you can hear
  • • 2 things you can smell
  • • 1 thing you're grateful for right now

Before you decide anything big

Urges pass, even when they don't feel like they will. You don't have to make a permanent decision because of what you're feeling right now. Give yourself 20 minutes, change your surroundings, and get another person involved.

  • • Call or text someone in your support system
  • • Get through the next hour — not the whole day
  • • Change your environment, even just the room you're in
  • • Put something between you and the impulsive decision — time, distance, a person

Reach out

You don't have to do this part alone.

In an emergency, call 911. If you're in immediate danger, having a medical emergency, or at risk of harming yourself or someone else, call 911 or go to the nearest emergency room — emergency responders can get help to you fastest.

If you need to talk to someone right now, call or text 988 (Suicide & Crisis Lifeline) — free, confidential, and available 24/7 in the U.S.

This page offers peer support, not emergency or clinical care.

What works without internet

Calling 911 or calling or texting 988 uses your phone service, not the internet, so the crisis numbers in the app work whenever your phone can make a call.

Things that need a connection: the Contact form, music videos, Facebook, the Etsy shop, books on Amazon, and outside recovery resources.

Updates

Your privacy

Privacy Policy

What this site keeps, what it sends, and what it doesn't do — in plain language.

Last updated:

The short version

  • Front Porch Recovery has no accounts, no ads, no analytics, and no tracking pixels, and it does not set its own cookies.
  • The Daily Check-In and Recovery Counter save a small amount of information in your own browser. It is never sent to Front Porch Recovery, and we can't see it.
  • If you use the Contact form, your message is delivered to us through a service called Formspree.
  • We don't sell or rent your information, and we don't share it for advertising.
  • Our web host and a few outside services receive basic technical information when the site loads.

Who we are

Front Porch Recovery is a peer-support, recovery education, lived-experience, publishing, music, community, and resource website run by . The website is located at . In this policy, “Front Porch Recovery,” “we,” and “us” mean Justin Whetstone and this website.

Front Porch Recovery is not a treatment center, medical provider, therapist, or crisis or emergency service. This policy covers this website only.

Information saved in your browser (not sent to us)

Some tools on this site remember things using your browser's built-in storage (called “local storage”). This information stays on the device and browser you used. It is not sent to Front Porch Recovery or anyone else, and we have no way to see it.

Daily Check-In. When you submit a check-in, your browser saves:

  • your total number of check-ins, the date of your last check-in, and your current streak; and
  • a short history of up to your 30 most recent check-ins: the date, the mood you picked, your craving/urge number, and the “need” and “commitment” options you selected.

What you type in the “honest thing” and “grateful for” boxes is not saved. It is shown back to you on the screen and disappears when you leave or reload the page.

Recovery Counter. If you enter a recovery start date, your browser saves that date so the counter still works the next time you visit.

A note about shared devices. Anyone who uses the same device and browser could open these tools and see your saved check-in totals, streak, or start date. To remove this information, clear this site's data in your browser settings (sometimes called “site data” or “cookies and site data”), or use a private/incognito window, which doesn't keep it after you close it.

Information you send us: the Contact form

If you use the Contact form, it collects your name, email address, the reason you picked, and your message. The form is processed by Formspree ↗, a third-party form service, which receives, stores, and delivers the message to us under its own privacy policy ↗.

We use what you send only to read and respond to your message. We don't add you to a mailing list because you contacted us, and we don't sell or rent your information.

Please don't send highly sensitive information

Front Porch Recovery does not intentionally ask for medical records, passwords, financial information, or other highly sensitive personal information through this website, and nothing on the site requires it. Please don't send those details through the Contact form or by email. If you choose to share something personal about your recovery or health in a message, it becomes part of that message, which is stored by Formspree and in our email inbox.

Newsletter / email signup (not active yet)

The newsletter signup on this site is not connected yet. Its button is turned off, and nothing you type there is sent anywhere.

If a newsletter is added later, the signup form will collect your first name and email address so we can send you Front Porch Recovery updates. That information would be handled by the email service we choose, under its own privacy policy, and every email would include a way to unsubscribe. This policy will be updated to name that service before the signup is turned on.

Technical information collected by hosting and outside services

Like almost every website, this one relies on a few outside services. When your browser connects to them, they may receive basic technical information such as your IP address, browser type, device type, and the page requested, and they handle it under their own policies:

  • GitHub Pages (hosting). The site is hosted on GitHub Pages. GitHub logs visitors' IP addresses for security purposes. See the GitHub Privacy Statement ↗.
  • Google Fonts. The site's typeface is loaded from Google's servers, so Google receives the request from your browser. See Google's Privacy Policy ↗.
  • YouTube videos. The Music page includes embedded YouTube players. When they load or play, YouTube (owned by Google) may collect information and set its own cookies under Google's Privacy Policy ↗.

Links to other websites

This site links to outside websites, including Facebook (our page and the Love Beyond the Chain community group), YouTube, Etsy, Amazon, and recovery-resource organizations such as SAMHSA, 988, USARA, AA, NA, SMART Recovery, and others. Those links open in a new tab and are marked as leaving the site.

Outside websites have their own privacy practices and policies, and Front Porch Recovery does not control them. Once you leave this site, their policies apply. Purchases you make on Amazon or Etsy are handled entirely by those companies; Front Porch Recovery never receives your payment information.

If you install the app

You can add Front Porch Recovery to your phone's home screen as an app. To let it open without internet, your device keeps a copy of the site's own public files (the page, icons, and font). That copy contains no personal information and is never sent anywhere. The Check-In and Recovery Counter work the same way in the app as on the website. Removing the app from your home screen, or clearing this site's data in your browser settings, deletes the copy.

Children

This site is written for adults and is not directed to children under 13. We don't knowingly collect personal information from children under 13 through the Contact form. If you believe a child has sent us personal information, please contact us and we will delete it.

Your choices

  • You can use the Check-In, Daily Porch, Toolbox, and Recovery Counter without giving us any personal information.
  • You can clear anything saved in your browser at any time, as described above.
  • You can ask us to delete a message you sent through the Contact form by emailing us. We'll delete it from our email, and we'll delete it from Formspree where our account allows it.

Changes to this policy

If the site's features change — for example, if the newsletter is connected or analytics are ever added — this policy will be updated first, and the “Last updated” date above will change.

2. What Front Porch Recovery is — and isn't

Front Porch Recovery shares peer support, recovery education, encouragement, lived-experience writing, books, music, community links, and general information.

Nothing on this site is medical advice, diagnosis, treatment, therapy, counseling, legal advice, or emergency or crisis care, and it is not a substitute for any of them. Always talk with a qualified doctor, mental health professional, or treatment provider about your health, medications, or stopping any substance. Stopping alcohol or certain medications suddenly can be medically dangerous. Don't ignore or delay professional advice because of something you read here.

3. Emergencies and crisis situations

This website is not monitored for emergencies and can't send help. If you are in an emergency or crisis, use emergency or crisis resources right away: call 911 for emergencies, or call or text 988 for suicide and crisis support in the U.S.

  • Recovery Counter. It does simple date math in your browser. It's a personal tool, not an official record.
  • Porch Stories. Stories reflect individual lived experiences. Some community stories use changed names to protect privacy. They aren't recommendations for how anyone else should recover.

You remain responsible for your own decisions and actions. Recovery looks different for everyone, and there is more than one pathway.

Affiliate Disclosure

How the links on this site work, and when money is involved.

Last updated:

How affiliate links work here

Some book, product, or resource links on Front Porch Recovery may be affiliate links. If you click an affiliate link and make an eligible purchase, Front Porch Recovery may receive a small commission from that company. There is no additional cost to you — the price is the same whether or not you use the link.

Where practical, affiliate links will be identified as affiliate links where they appear, and this page will list every affiliate program the site takes part in.

Not every outside link is an affiliate link

Most outside links on this site earn nothing. Recovery resources listed in the Toolbox — such as SAMHSA, 988, USARA, AA, NA, SMART Recovery, and Al-Anon — are shared because they're useful. No one pays to be listed, and those links are not affiliate links.

Front Porch Recovery's own books and products

Links to Front Porch Recovery's own books, Etsy products, music, and other products are not automatically affiliate links. When you buy one of those, the money comes from the sale of Justin Whetstone's own work (for books, that's an author royalty paid by the publishing platform) — not from an affiliate commission. We just want you to know plainly that those links support Front Porch Recovery.

Sponsored content

Nothing on this site is currently sponsored or paid for by another company. If that ever changes, the sponsored content will be clearly labeled where it appears.

Our message stays the same

Affiliate relationships don't change the purpose or message of Front Porch Recovery. Things are recommended here because we believe they could genuinely help someone in recovery — never because a link might earn a commission.
